g: HOW TO STOP WORRYING AND START LIVING · LESSON 7 Forget yourself by helping others. <<<<<<< HEAD The surest cure for worry is caring about someone else.

g.text: Worry grows in a closed room.
The longer we stare at our troubles, the bigger and darker they get.
Alfred Adler, a famous Austrian psychiatrist, had one daily rule.
Each morning, think how you could
bring some pleasure to someone else.
Her world shrank to one bed.
Margaret Tayler Yates, a naval officer’s wife in Hawaii.
A phone by her bed made her a contact point for frightened families.
Comforting strangers got her out of bed.
MORE TIME OUT OF BED THAN IN IT
Helping others pulls together everything Carnegie teaches.
THE ONLY DAY YOU CAN ACTUALLY LIVE
OTHERS’ STRUGGLES PUT YOURS IN VIEW
You do not need a crisis to try this.

g:
Who could you make a little happier each morning?
14 DAYS
FOURTEEN DAYS · THEN GO DO IT AND WATCH YOUR WORRIES ======= The surprising worry cure that starts with someone else.

g.text: Worry loves an audience of one.
When we brood, attention circles back to our own fears.
Carnegie’s answer: turn your attention outward.
Psychiatrist Alfred Adler’s advice for gloomy patients.
Margaret Tayler Yates spent most days in bed with heart trouble.
Hour after hour, she calmed anxious military families.
No crisis needed: take a real interest in the people you meet.
Each small kindness pulls your mind off your own troubles.
Your mind can only hold so much at one time.
One habit ties it all together.
Helping connects many of Carnegie’s other ideas.
Worry shrinks when your life points outward.

g:
One small kindness. Every single day. For fourteen days.
THEN NOTICE WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR WORRIES
